guard: the connector never returns - on startup failure or graceful stop - while the private Jcode daemon tree it launched is still executing; teardown is proven from the seat's own records with bounded SIGTERM then exact-PID/group SIGKILL escalation, and a survivor is a thrown error, never a clean report
_note: assert-and-die suite: a red run can never print the PASSED banner, so completion is guarded by the tick floor (the target assertions sit at marks 4 and 5 of 9), not a completionMarker.
why: A live seat hit a readiness refusal at startup; the host exited non-zero, the manager retired
the seat's mesh credential, and the private `jcode serve` daemon it had launched kept running
unmanaged - own session, own MCP child, holding the seat's private home (#839). The SDK's only
daemon stop is a servers.json lookup that must match the alias socket path VERBATIM; a
canonicalized entry (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp) or a wiped registry is a silent no-op, and
killing the bridge never reaches the setsid daemon. The fake daemon here registers with the
canonicalized home path - the measured miss shape - so only the connector's own record-driven
teardown can turn the suite green.
The mutations attack the three legs that make the teardown honest: the call itself (the shipped
defect was exactly its absence), the record reader that names the daemon (servers.json +
active_pids are the only place the setsid daemon's PID exists), and the group signal (the MCP
child is NOT recorded anywhere - it dies only because the daemon's setsid group is signalled,
so degrading group-kill to exact-PID leaves it orphaned and only the MCP-child assertion sees it).
